 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. DETROIT (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is active against the Detroit Lions , putting him on the field Sunday for the first time since he pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend.
 The three-time Pro Bowl running back was recently removed from the commissioner's exempt list , which had prevented him from playing in the first six games of the season or practicing with the team.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Green Bay's running game desperately needs a boost. Entering the game in Detroit, the Packers ranked last in the NFL in rushing yards and yards per carry.
 Jacobs expressed contrition on Wednesday when he returned to practice and spoke to reporters for the first time since the altercation with his then-girlfriend, during which she said he threw her to the ground.
 Jacobs declined to discuss specifics of his case, adding he hoped to use the situation as an opportunity to grow into a better person.
 "Obviously, man, I'm remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation," Jacobs said. "Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The NFL had placed Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list on Aug. 30, shortly after charges were filed against him. In September, he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property.
 The league is still investigating Jacobs over the incident and could hand out more discipline.
 "I thought I'd be playing sooner," Jacobs said. "But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I'm just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn't want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I'm just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing."
 The Raiders drafted the former Alabama star with the No. 24 pick in 2019, and he signed with Green Bay as a free agent in 2024.
 Jacobs ran for 7,803 yards and 74 touchdowns from his rookie year through last season and had 269 career catches for 2,072 yards and two scores.
